Hi Sarah — great to meet you both earlier. Appreciate the clear list; summarizing below and proposing next steps.

Summary of options (what we typically see):
- Marketplace (AWS/GCP/Azure) — supported. For enterprise customers we often enable a Private Offer on AWS (or an equivalent on other clouds) so procurement can accept a single consolidated invoice and retain cloud billing alignment. This path requires ~2-3 weeks of enablement work for entitlements/metering plus marketplace vendor onboarding.
- Direct PO (invoice) — Redwood can invoice Bluecrest directly on NET30 or NET45 terms depending on negotiation. This is the fastest path for organizations that require a PO on file.
- Card / self-serve — immediate for small pilots; recommended when teams need to start a POC ASAP and want to avoid marketplace lead times.

Key notes for your teams:
- Marketplace private offer provisioning is typically handled by our Marketplace Ops + Partnerships team (they do the SKU/entitlement mapping). I will loop Karthik for technical enablement and Marissa for billing/ops.
- For a PO: we need a filled PO with billing address + remit to, a signed Master Services Agreement (we can provide a redline-friendly template), and a contact for invoice routing. Typical legal turnaround we see is 1–3 weeks for smaller redlines; complex SOWs can take longer.

Attached: Redwood_PO_Process_FAQ.pdf (short bullets on PO steps), Marketplace_Enablement_Checklist.xlsx (what our vendor team needs), AWS_PrivateOffer_Steps.docx (illustrative).

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share the PO process FAQ + marketplace checklist (attached).
2) Karthik will follow up with a brief technical checklist / timing for Private Offer metering and entitlements.
3) If Bluecrest prefers PO and wants to target a pilot start in early Sept, please send your PO template and preferred invoice terms — we’ll draft an invoice-term sheet and MSA redline to speed Legal.

If the lowest-friction path is desired, start the POC on a card and then convert to PO/Marketplace for production. Happy to sync tomorrow if helpful.

Thanks Logan — looping in a few technical clarifications from the enablement side.

Quick technical checklist for Marketplace Private Offer provisioning:
- SKU/entitlement mapping: need expected seat/throughput tiers and approx token/month consumption so we can map to metered SKUs.
- Region & account mapping: confirm which AWS accounts/regions you want the offer to cover (us-east-1 by default).
- Metering hooks: we provide the metrics endpoint and need ~48–72 hours to validate sample consumption data.
- Billing cadence: Marketplace supports monthly usage billing; Redwood will reconcile and invoice via the marketplace for Private Offers.

Timing note: enabling a Private Offer and getting it visible in the marketplace catalog can take 2–3 weeks (vendor onboarding + entitlements testing). If Bluecrest is aiming for an early-September pilot, card-based POC + parallel marketplace enablement is the safest path.

If helpful I can join a short procurement call with your team to walk through entitlements and what we need from a PO vs. marketplace perspective.

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
